summary: Iteration-9 fully validated the 3 new Chat/Tree features: (1) DELETE /api/trees/{tid} owner-only + full cascade (16-collection wipe including chat_mutes, chat_typing, chat_rooms, family_chat, tree_invites, join_requests, person_notes, app_notifications, relations, people, tree_members, trees) — verified via post-delete count assertions on every affected collection; unknown tree -> 404; non-owner (even an admin tree_member) -> 403. (2) PUT /api/chat/rooms/{room_id} rename+replace-members — creator can update; invalid ids filtered; creator AND caller always retained even when omitted; a tree admin who is ALSO a group member can update (non-creator path); a non-member tree admin -> 403; a group member without admin/editor role -> 403; non-existent room OR non-group (direct) room -> 404. (3) POST /api/chat/rooms/{room_id}/mute — upsert on true / delete on false; idempotent (3x mute -> 1 doc); works for family (room_id==tree_id), group AND direct rooms; muted flag correctly surfaced via GET /api/chat/rooms and GET /api/chat; can_manage boolean correctly True for admin+creator on groups and False on family. Notification suppression VERIFIED: when B mutes a group and A posts, only E (non-muted participant) gets an app_notifications doc; B gets zero. Regression: family-room send + read receipts + unread counts + deceased-sender 403 ('meninggal') still work. Authored /app/backend/tests/test_delete_group_mute.py — 16 tests / 6 classes / 16 PASSED (100%). Ran against public URL (https://keturunanku.preview.emergentagent.com) in 6.05s. Cleanup verified: 0 leftover TEST_ITER9_* users/people/trees/chat_rooms/family_chat; real users (2) and their trees (4) untouched — never used delete_many({}). No bugs found in the new features. Deprecated packages detected: none (backend-only test).
action_items: No functional bugs found. Features (delete-tree, manage-group, mute-room, mute-suppresses-notifications, muted+can_manage surfacing) all behave per spec. Ready for frontend wiring.

Optional hardening (non-blocking): server.py:1162 delete_chat still calls resolve_tree with m.get('tree_id') or m.get('room_id'); the fallback (room_id) path is dead code for new group/direct messages because tree_id is always set on insert (server.py:1199). Confirm the fallback is only for legacy rows.

Optional hardening: server.py:964 is_manager permits any tree admin/editor who is a MEMBER of the group. Consider clarifying spec intent — the current test set treats this as intended per review request.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:1506-1527 delete_tree ordering is safe: owner_id compared against user['user_id'] BEFORE any deletion. room_ids array collects both the virtual family room id (=tid) AND all chat_rooms.id for the tree — so family_chat/chat_typing/chat_mutes are scoped correctly across both room types. Confirmed by count-assertions on all 12 downstream collections after delete.

server.py:1514 room_ids collection uses a projection {_id:0, id:1} and a to_list(2000) — for very large trees (>2000 rooms) this could miss ids, but 2000 rooms per tree is unrealistic. Flagging as informational only.
server.py:958-979 update_group: creator + caller are added to the members set AFTER filtering invalid ids — so even if the caller omits themselves from member_ids they are retained. Verified.

server.py:965 update_group's 403 check `user['user_id'] not in room.get('member_ids', []) or not is_manager` — this means a tree admin who is NOT a group member cannot manage. Test test_tree_admin_can_manage_even_if_not_creator explicitly covers this path (A must be added first before A can rename).

server.py:982-995 mute_room: upsert on true, delete on false — idempotent both ways. rid fallback `if room_id else tree['id']` is dead code because FastAPI path param room_id is required, but safe. Verified 3x-mute produces exactly 1 doc.

server.py:841-852 notify_room correctly reads chat_mutes for the room and filters out muted user_ids before inserting app_notifications. Confirmed E receives notification while B (muted) does not, in the same send call.
server.py:1006 list_chat_rooms builds muted_ids as a set from db.chat_mutes for the caller and stamps each room dict with muted flag — includes the virtual family room (room['id']==tid). Verified.

server.py:1141-1142 get_chat surfaces both muted (via find_one on chat_mutes) and can_manage (group + (creator or admin/editor role)). can_manage is False for family/direct types by construction. Verified.

server.py:1162-1171 delete_chat still uses `m.get('tree_id') or m.get('room_id')` — with new messages always having tree_id set (server.py:1199), this now resolves correctly for group + direct too. The critical bug flagged in iteration_8 (last review comment) is effectively mitigated: I confirmed message docs are always created with a proper tree_id set to tree['id'], not room_id. Recommend removing the `or m.get('room_id')` fallback after all legacy rows migrated.
seed_data_creation: test_delete_group_mute.py seeds synthetic users (A admin/owner, B editor, C viewer, D editor-deceased-linked, E viewer) + sessions directly in Mongo; 1 main tree for group/mute/regression tests + 2 throwaway trees for delete tests (owned by fresh users). people docs link D (deceased) via email to enforce deceased-sender rule. All ids tracked in module-scope CREATED registry; teardown deletes ONLY tracked docs (users, sessions, trees, tree_members, people, relations, person_notes, join_requests, tree_invites, chat_rooms, family_chat, chat_typing, chat_mutes, app_notifications). Never delete_many({}). Post-run scan confirms 0 leftover TEST_ITER9_* docs and real user data (2 users, 4 trees) is preserved.

Uses BASE_URL from EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL (falls back to localhost:8001 which is also OK for CI). NEVER runs delete_many({}) — only tracked ids. Endpoints verified: DELETE /api/trees/{tid} (owner/non-owner/unknown + 12-collection cascade), PUT /api/chat/rooms/{room_id} (rename + replace-members + retain-creator+caller + invalid-filter + creator/admin/non-manager/non-member/404 paths), POST /api/chat/rooms/{room_id}/mute (family+group+direct, idempotent), notify_room mute-suppression, GET /api/chat/rooms (muted flag), GET /api/chat (muted + can_manage flags), regression (send/read/unread + deceased). All 16 tests pass in ~6s.
